A.explanation: With $v \approx 23.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $s = 1200 \text{ m}$, $a = v^2/(2s) \approx 0.23 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: About twice too large, obtained if $v^2/s$ is used instead of $v^2/(2s)$ for motion from rest.

C.explanation: Obtained if $85 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ is substituted directly as $85 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ without converting to $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Obtained if the speed is left in $\text{km h}^{-1}$ and the factor 2 in $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ is also omitted.

hints: Notice the mixed units: take-off speed is $85 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ but distance is $1.20 \text{ km}$ and acceleration must be in $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so both need conversion to metres and seconds.
Connect initial speed $u = 0$, final speed $v$ and distance $s$ with the no-time equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, then rearrange for $a$.
First calculate $v = 85 \times 1000/3600 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $s = 1200 \text{ m}$, then evaluate $a = v^2/(2s)$ and check the unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: List the SUVAT data in SI units: $u = 0$, $s = 1.20 \text{ km} = 1200 \text{ m}$, and $v = 85 \text{ km h}^{-1}$ to be converted.
Convert the final speed: $v = 85 \times (1000/3600) \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 23.6 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Select $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ because time $t$ is unknown and acceleration is constant, then rearrange to $a = (v^2 - u^2)/(2s) = v^2/(2s)$.
Using the full $1.20 \text{ km}$ gives the smallest acceleration that still reaches take-off speed, so this minimum value matches the smallest option. This is option A.
